newsitem.title: USA: Maytag profits down, says Montgomery Ward owes $39 million.
newsitem.headline: Maytag profits down, says Montgomery Ward owes $39 million.

text.p: Maytag Corp. said Thursday its second-quarter profits edged lower from record levels, but remained strong as demand continued to grow for its appliances, floor care products, and vending and commercial laundry equipment.
Maytag also said that retailer Montgomery Ward Holding Corp., which filed for bankruptcy July 7, owes it about $39 million in accounts receivables.
"It is too early to determine when and to what extent the amount due from Montgomery Ward will be recovered," Maytag Chairman Leonard Hadley said in a news release.

"Based on information currently available, we have a reserve for the portion of this account we consider to be at risk. We continue to evaluate this situation and are having discussions with Montgomery Ward regarding our relationship as they restructure their business, operating under the auspices of bankruptcy court," Hadley added.

Maytag said its net income fell to $43.8 million, or 45 cents a share, in the second quarter from a record $44.3 million, or 43 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Per-share results in 1997 were based on about 6 percent fewer shares.
Sales grew to $814.5 million from $754.6 million, including $26.3 million in the second quarter from a China joint venture formed last fall.
"Looking ahead, we continue to believe 1997 will be another good year for Maytag," Hadley said.
New products and models should help generate higher sales in the second half of this year, and some costs associated with the new product initiatives will drop, Maytag said.

Sales of Hoover brand floor care products and Dixie-Narco vending equipment continued to be strong in the second quarter, and Maytag's commercial laundry equipment business benefited from launch of a horizontal-axis washer, it said.
Sales were up for Maytag International, which handles export sales and licensing agreements.
"Major appliances, our largest product category, posted a slight sales increase for the quarter in an intensely competitive business environment," Hadley said.
Sales of new Maytag and Jenn-Air brand refrigerators were exceptionally strong. Maytag laundry equipment and dishwashers, plus Magic Chef cooking appliances, also saw quarterly gains in unit sales.
However, there was some weakness in other branded product categories and in private label sales, Hadley said.

Operating income for major home appliances was depressed by costs associated with the initial production of new products, aggressive merchandising programmes and setting up regional product distribution centres, he said.
Newton, Iowa-based Maytag's stock rose 12.5 cents to $27.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
